items.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Ahmad Jamal, Errol Garner, Art Blakey... I learned from everybody, you know?

ctx.x: You learn what not to play — I’m not going to play like that.

No, I’ve had many experiences. Ahmad Jamal, Errol Garner, Art Blakey, Count Basie, Ella Fitzgerald, Louis Armstrong, you know, it goes on and on, Charlie Mingus, you know, and Shearing. Dave Brubeck, he had that big hit when I was in high school. Ellington, everybody. I learned from everybody, you know? Ervin, Billy Eckstine, they were all you know, they were making music in those days. They were nice times. Even Theresa Brewer and Frankie Laine, I listened to them, you know? The Four Lads, The Platters, the…

items.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Erroll Garner couldn’t read a note. None of those people could read. So that’s how we grew up.

ctx.x: But that in itself is an education, isn’t it?

That was my education. And a lot of Pittsburgers don’t know anything about, you know, math as far as music and technical things. Erroll Garner couldn’t read a note. None of those people could read. So that’s how we grew up. Well Pittsburgh had that thing happening anyway because of all of the corporate home offices. At that time there was the large home offices for private big businesses like Gulf and Westinghouse’s home office was there, U.S. Steel, Jones & Laughlin, you had Rockwell, you had Heinz. You had 54…
I learned about jazz in Pittsburgh at The Encore, listening to Harold Betters.
